title: Turkey Meatballs & White Bean Marinara over Whole Wheat Pasta
description: Lean turkey meatballs simmered in a white bean marinara over whole wheat pasta. High protein, high fiber, and genuinely filling.

instructions.text: Mix the meatballs: in a large bowl, combine ground turkey, panko, egg, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined — overmixing makes them tough.
Form into 12-14 meatballs about 1.5 inches each. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add meatballs and sear on all sides until browned but not cooked through, about 5 minutes total. Work in batches if needed — don't crowd the pot.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, cannellini beans, oregano, basil, red pepper flakes, and salt, nestling the meatballs into the sauce. Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook 20-25 minutes until meatballs reach 165°F internally.
About 10 minutes before the sauce is done, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Divide pasta between bowls, top with meatballs and sauce, and finish with torn fresh basil.

notes: Use no-salt-added crushed tomatoes — it's the single biggest sodium lever in this recipe and drops ~300-400mg per serving. Regular crushed tomatoes push one bowl close to 50% of daily sodium. Meatballs freeze well raw or cooked if you want to double the batch. Whole wheat pasta holds al dente texture much better than brown rice pasta — go by package directions, no need to watch the clock tightly.
